issues.legal_issue: A judgment pronounced after a party dies between the conclusion of the hearing and pronouncement is not rendered ineffective by the party’s death.
material_facts: The plaintiff died after arguments in the appeal had concluded and the judgment had been reserved.
The plaintiff’s counsel notified the appellate court of the death and sought time to bring the legal representatives on record.
The appellate court declined the request and pronounced judgment.
issues.conclusion: The death did not cause abatement, and the appellate judgment was not a nullity.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXII Rule 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that there is no abatement when a party dies between the conclusion of the hearing and pronouncement of judgment, whether or not the cause of action survives; the judgment may be pronounced and has the same force and effect as if pronounced before the death. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.judgment_pending_after_hearing: The proceeding’s hearing has concluded and judgment remains to be pronounced.
predicates.party_dies_before_pronouncement: A party to the proceeding dies after the hearing concludes but before judgment is pronounced.

issues.definition: When judgment is pending after the hearing and a party dies before its pronouncement, the judgment remains effective.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser seeking specific performance must prove continuous readiness and willingness to perform the purchaser’s essential contractual obligations, and the court may refuse the discretionary remedy when the purchaser’s capacity and conduct do not establish that readiness and willingness.
material_facts: The plaintiff agreed to purchase a house, paid an advance, and took possession as a tenant pending execution of the sale deed.
The plaintiff did not pay a further contracted advance intended to discharge a mortgage debt; that amount was adjusted toward rent with consent.
The plaintiff failed to pay rent as agreed and had substantial rent arrears.
The plaintiff had limited funds and other financial obligations, and the courts found that he lacked the means to complete the purchase.
Although a witness offered to lend the plaintiff money, the witness did not have the money available and would have had to raise it by mortgaging property.
After being directed to deposit the required amount or furnish a bank guarantee, the plaintiff did neither.
The trial court found that the plaintiff was not ready and willing to perform, and the appellate court affirmed that finding.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff failed to establish continuous readiness and willingness to perform the contract, so the refusal of specific performance was upheld and the special leave petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, a plaintiff seeking specific performance must plead and prove performance or continuous readiness and willingness to perform the essential terms of the contract that the plaintiff must perform, except terms whose performance was prevented or waived by the defendant. Readiness and willingness are assessed from the plaintiff’s conduct before and after filing suit and the attending circumstances; the consideration must be shown to have been available, although the plaintiff need not keep the money physically on hand if the plaintiff has the capacity to raise it. Under Section 20, specific performance is an equitable discretionary remedy and is not automatic merely because a valid agreement exists. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: specific_performance_claim and (funding_capacity_unproved or failed_funding_direction) and contractual_obligations_unperformed

predicates.specific_performance_claim: A purchaser brought a proceeding seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.funding_capacity_unproved: The purchaser’s evidence and financial circumstances did not establish the capacity to raise the funds required to complete the purchase.
predicates.failed_funding_direction: The purchaser did not deposit the required funds or provide the requested security after the court directed the purchaser to do so.
predicates.contractual_obligations_unperformed: The purchaser failed to perform material contractual obligations, including payment obligations, and the purchaser’s conduct did not show continuing readiness to perform.

issues.definition: When a purchaser seeks specific performance but does not establish funding capacity or comply with a funding direction, and has left material contractual obligations unperformed, specific performance is denied.
